beats.narration_text: Last episode, ECIS was four readers and one triangulator on two tickers. I'm Anjana — here's the same system, six months later, running at a scale that actually matters.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: greeting 'Hello, Anjana'; ask types itself
runningText 'loading season two…'
output lines resolve: 'two LLMs voting instead of one' / 'twenty-five companies, one scorecard' / 'a live dashboard, not a report'

props.command: Last time, ECIS read earnings calls with four readers and one triangulator. Now the system runs at real scale — two LLMs voting instead of one, twenty-five companies instead of two, and a live dashboard tying it all together. Can you show me how it grew?
output: two LLMs voting instead of one
a live dashboard, not a report

beats.narration_text: ECIS reads earnings calls with four independent readers and one triangulator. That was version one. Here is what it looks like now.

show.event: the four-reader architecture diagram appears instantly, fully formed — keyword, FinBERT, NER, LLM feeding the triangulator
hold — recognizable callback to Episode 1
camera pulls back; the diagram shrinks into a corner of a larger, dimmed frame — teasing what's coming

beats.narration_text: The LLM reader used to be one model. Now it is two. Llama and Mistral process every chunk independently through the same pipeline, the same prompts, the same self-consistency checks. They do not share answers. The triangulator weighs both. When they agree, confidence goes up. When they disagree, the system knows exactly where the language is ambiguous.

show.event: the LLM node splits cleanly into two: 'Llama 3.1 8B' (purple) and 'Mistral 7B' (teal), both fed by the same chunk stream
a chunk flows in; Llama outputs 'raised 0.85', Mistral outputs 'raised 0.82'; green 'AGREE' line connects them; triangulator outputs 'raised 0.88' — confidence boosted
a second chunk flows in; Llama outputs 'maintained 0.71', Mistral outputs 'raised 0.68'; red 'DISAGREE' line connects them; triangulator outputs 'raised 0.54' with an amber indicator
both nodes settle side by side, pulsing steadily; label lands: 'Two architectures. One triangulator.'

beats.narration_text: The pipeline now runs across twenty to twenty-five companies. Hundreds of transcripts, thousands of chunks, all flowing through the same four readers, the same routing, the same scorecard. What started on two tickers is now watching a full sector.

show.event: the two-model architecture shrinks to a small icon at center
numbered company nodes fade in one by one around it in a circle — 22 total, no names shown
glowing data lines connect each node to the center; particles flow inward; counters climb: 'Transcripts: 200+' / 'Chunks processed: 10,000+'
the first two nodes briefly highlight brighter than the rest — on 'started on two tickers'
all nodes pulse simultaneously — on 'full sector'

beats.narration_text: At this scale, the hardest call is not raised or lowered. It is the line between maintained and nothing. A CEO says "we are comfortable with our current outlook." Is that guidance maintained, or is that just a sentence? The system now draws that boundary precisely. Maintained means the company actively reaffirmed. Nothing means there was no guidance at all.

show.event: left card fades in: 'We are reaffirming our full-year revenue outlook of twelve billion dollars.' — tag 'MAINTAINED' in blue, confidence 0.82
right card fades in: 'We remain focused on executing our strategy.' — tag 'NONE' in grey, confidence 0.91
the dividing line between the cards pulses and glows; label lands: 'The Boundary'
text lands below: 'Maintained = actively reaffirmed. None = no guidance at all.'

props.leftQuote: We are reaffirming our full-year revenue outlook of twelve billion dollars.
props.rightQuote: We remain focused on executing our strategy.

beats.narration_text: Everything lands in one place. Every signal, every reader's vote, every calibration curve, every model's performance, and every decision the feedback loops make. Not a report generated after the fact. A live system you can query, drill into, and interrogate.

show.event: panel 1 (top-left): signal explorer table — rows populate with ticker, direction, confidence
panel 2 (top-right): calibration curve, now with two lines — purple Llama, teal Mistral — drawing against the diagonal
panel 3 (bottom-left): model comparison bar chart — grouped purple/teal bars per metric, growing upward
panel 4 (bottom-right): agent activity timeline — event dots appear with labels ('recalibration triggered', 'weight adjusted')
all four panels visible at once, subtly alive — numbers ticking, curves redrawing

props.sparkLine: Query it. Don't wait for the report.

beats.narration_text: Two models. Twenty-five companies. One scorecard that never looks away. ECIS, episode two.

show.event: flash 1: dual Llama/Mistral node (purple + teal) — on 'two models'
flash 2: ticker grid, all pulsing — on 'twenty-five companies'
flash 3: dual-line calibration curve — on 'one scorecard'
title lands center screen: 'ECIS — Episode 2'

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. The LLM reader is now two independent models, cross-checked against each other. The pipeline covers twenty-five companies, not two. The system draws a precise line between maintained guidance and no guidance at all. And everything lands live, in one queryable dashboard.

show.event: 0.5s lead pause, then ClaudeVerdictArtifact card builds in
line 1: dual-model icon settles in
line 2: ticker-grid icon settles in
line 3: boundary-line icon settles in
line 4: dashboard icon locks in, largest element

artifactLines: The LLM reader is now two independent models, cross-checked.
The pipeline covers twenty-five companies, not two.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. "I have one process at work where I trust a single judgment call — one model, one reviewer, one gut check — and I've never questioned whether that's enough. Can you help me: one, figure out what a genuine second, independent check would look like for that specific call; two, define what counts as 'agreement' versus 'disagreement' between the two; and three, tell me honestly whether the disagreement case is rare enough that adding a second check isn't worth the cost?" Paste that into Claude and see whether your own single-model process has a Llama-and-Mistral problem hiding in it.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: greeting 'Your turn.'; prompt types itself into the composer
runningText 'checking for a hidden single point of failure…'
